root_cause.text: The `need_futex_hash_allocate_default()` function incorrectly required both `CLONE_THREAD` and `CLONE_VM` flags together, causing per-CPU futex hash allocations to be skipped for non-pthread clones that share the mm, leading to use-after-free when the `mm->futex_ref` counter is incremented on a stale per-CPU allocation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the condition from `(clone_flags & (CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_VM)) != (CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_VM)` to `(clone_flags & (CLONE_VM | CLONE_VFORK)) == CLONE_VM`. The CVE description explicitly states that the strict `CLONE_THREAD` requirement "breaks the non-concurrency assumptions when doing the mm->futex_ref pcpu allocations" when the mm is shared via other clone methods, resulting in "the +1 bias can end up on a percpu counter that mm->futex_ref no longer points at" (slab-use-after-free). The fix broadens allocation to any `CLONE_VM` clone except `vfork()`, ensuring the per-CPU counter is properly allocated whenever the address space is shared.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `need_futex_hash_allocate_default()` contains the vulnerable logic. It checks `if ((clone_flags & (CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_VM)) != (CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_VM))` which requires BOTH flags to be set together. This is the root cause: it incorrectly skips futex hash allocation for non-pthread clones that share the mm (which have CLONE_VM but not CLONE_THREAD). The condition should allow allocation when CLONE_VM is set (indicating mm sharing), regardless of CLONE_THREAD status. The current logic returns false (skips allocation) for any clone that doesn't have both flags, which means clones with only CLONE_VM will not get the futex hash allocated, leading to the use-after-free vulnerability described. The fix is not present in this commit - it introduces the buggy function.
